summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436, a network destination is reconstructed at runtime via String.fromCharCode(...) rather than appearing as a plain string. The decoded byte sequence resolves to the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. Obfuscating a hardcoded outbound destination inside a WhatsApp session/message-send code path — where BIP-style credentials, session tokens, and message content are handled — is the shape of covert exfiltration to a non-first-party host, not legitimate library behavior. The destination is not documented, is not the caller's configured endpoint, and the char-code reconstruction is characteristic of anti-analysis rather than any benign use.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
